name: Arcanist
description:
Masters of Structure, Authors of the Unfinished

Arcanists approach magic as a system to be understood, mapped, and ultimately rewritten. Through disciplined study and formal instruction, they learn the underlying structures that govern spells: how energy flows, how space bends, how symbols compel reality to behave. To an Arcanist, magic is not mysterious—it is unfinished.

Rather than specializing in a single expression of power, Arcanists cultivate breadth over intensity, assembling solutions from many traditions at once. Their spells favor preparation, control, and inevitability, constructing advantages long before a conflict begins. Where others react, Arcanists anticipate. Where others improvise, Arcanists architect.

At the highest levels, master Arcanists cease to merely cast spells at all, instead authoring new ones, expanding the known boundaries of magic itself.

Magic is a language.
Arcanists are the ones adding new grammar.

Domains of Magic

Arcanists excel at magic that is deliberate, constructed, and systemic:

  • Spatial manipulation: teleportation, extradimensional spaces, gravity

  • Force and containment: barriers, wards, suspension, suppression

  • Transformation and fabrication: reshaping matter and form

  • Arcane logistics: shelters, storage, servants, magical infrastructure

  • Meta-magic: countering, dispelling, identifying, and rewriting spells

  • Reality overrides: time, simulacra, and wish-level effects

Taboo: Faith Without Understanding

Arcanists refuse to accept magic without comprehension. Power justified by tradition, destiny, or divine authority alone is deeply suspect.

Magic must be knowable—or it is unfinished.

Fault Lines

  • Votaries outsource understanding; Wildhearts romanticize ignorance.

  • Arcanists see themselves as responsible innovators—and are often seen as dangerous meddlers.
